summary:
A window can be made one colour with `length − (count of its most common colour)` repaints. Slide a window with
colour counts, shrinking when that exceeds `k`. Refinement: keep `maxf` as the highest count ever seen; the
answer only improves when `maxf` grows, so the window never needs to shrink, only slide. O(n).

question.md:
Repaint at most `k` tiles of `s`. Return the longest run of consecutive tiles that can end up one colour.

- **n up to 10⁵**, 26 colours.

think.md:
`"ABAABBBAB"`, `k = 1` → **5**.

For a fixed run, the cheapest choice is to keep its most common colour and repaint everything else, so it
needs `length − maxCount` repaints. Shrinking a valid run keeps it valid, so this is a longest-window problem.

The subtle refinement: we only care about windows **longer** than the best so far. A longer valid window needs
a larger `maxCount` than we've ever had. So `maxf` may safely be a historical maximum: while it's stale, the
window just slides at its current length and can't produce a wrong (too large) answer.

idea.md: For each start, extend while `length − maxCount ≤ k`, updating counts and `maxCount` incrementally.

lines.text: Add tiles, keeping counts and the top count; stop when the repaints needed (`length − top`) exceed `k`.

complexity.md: **Time O(n²)** in the worst case (large `k`). **Space O(1)** (26 counters).

steps.text: Start 0: the window grows to 0..3 (length 4). Adding B at 4 would break the rule, so this start stops.
Start 1: the window grows to 1..3 (length 3). Adding B at 4 would break the rule, so this start stops.
Start 2: the window grows to 2..4 (length 3). Adding B at 5 would break the rule, so this start stops.
Start 3: the window grows to 3..6 (length 4). Adding A at 7 would break the rule, so this start stops.
Start 4: the window grows to 4..8 (length 5). It reaches the end.
Start 5: the window grows to 5..8 (length 4). It reaches the end.
Starts 6..8 are checked the same way. The longest window starts at 4. In total about 38 cells were re-read, which grows like n²: the same cells are scanned again from every start.
Longest: 5.

walk.title: From each start, extend while the tiles that differ from the most common colour are at most k.

limits.md: Each start rebuilds its counts from nothing. One window that grows on the right and shrinks on the left reuses them.

approaches.title: Sliding window, recount the top colour

idea.md: Add `s[r]` to the counts. While `length − max(count) > k`, remove `s[left]` and advance. Track the longest window.

lines.text: Too many repaints: drop tiles from the left. The top count is recomputed over 26 colours each check.

steps.text: R adds A at 0; the rule still holds, so the window just grows to 0..0. New best: 1.
R adds B at 1; the rule still holds, so the window just grows to 0..1. New best: 2.
R adds A at 2; the rule still holds, so the window just grows to 0..2. New best: 3.
R adds A at 3; the rule still holds, so the window just grows to 0..3. New best: 4.
R adds B at 4. That breaks the rule (repaints 2). L moves past 0..1 until it holds again: window 2..4.
R adds B at 5. That breaks the rule (repaints 2). L moves past 2..2 until it holds again: window 3..5.
R adds B at 6; the rule still holds, so the window just grows to 3..6.
R adds A at 7. That breaks the rule (repaints 2). L moves past 3..3 until it holds again: window 4..7.
R adds B at 8; the rule still holds, so the window just grows to 4..8. New best: 5.
R visited each index once and L only ever moved right, so the pointers made at most 18 moves in total: O(n).
Longest: 5.

walk.title: Window with colour counts: a window works when its length minus its most common colour's count is at most k. Shrink from the left whenever it doesn't.

limits.md: Recomputes the top count over all 26 colours on every check. It doesn't need to be exact: a historical maximum is enough.

approaches.title: Window that never shrinks (historical max)

idea.md: Keep `maxf` = largest count seen in any window so far. After adding `s[r]`, if `length − maxf > k`, remove one tile from the left (the window slides at constant length). The final window length (or the max seen) is the answer.

build: Grow; slide by one if too long for `maxf`.

lines.text: Only the colour just added can raise the maximum.
If the window is one too long for `maxf`, drop one tile: the window keeps its length and moves right. `maxf` isn't lowered; a smaller value could never give a longer window anyway.
The window length only grows when a colour reaches a new `maxf`.

steps.text: Add 'A': maxf = 1. Fits, so the window grows. Length 1.
Add 'B': maxf = 1. Fits, so the window grows. Length 2.
Add 'A': maxf = 2. Fits, so the window grows. Length 3.
Add 'A': maxf = 3. Fits, so the window grows. Length 4.
Add 'B': maxf = 3. Too many repaints for that, so slide (left +1). Length 4.
Add 'B': maxf = 3. Too many repaints for that, so slide (left +1). Length 4.
Add 'B': maxf = 3. Too many repaints for that, so slide (left +1). Length 4.
Add 'A': maxf = 3. Too many repaints for that, so slide (left +1). Length 4.
Add 'B': maxf = 4. Fits, so the window grows. Length 5.
Longest: 5.

walk.title: Keep maxf = the highest count ever seen. The window never shrinks: when it's too big for maxf, it slides one step right. It grows only when some colour beats maxf.

takeaways.md:
- **"Make a window uniform with ≤ k changes":** cost = length − most frequent count.
- When you only want the maximum length, the window may **slide instead of shrink**, and a stale maximum is fine.
- Same template as "longest run of 1s with k flips".
